newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ dollar closes stronger after choppy session.
newsitem.headline: NZ dollar closes stronger after choppy session.

text.p: The New Zealand dollar closed higher on Tuesday after a choppy session.
Dealers said it may be nearing a near-term top but the local market remains short.
It ended at US$0.6865/72 from its 0.6841/48 opening, while the Trade-Weighted Index ended at 68.22, well up from its 67.99 opening.
Dealers said the kiwi dipped on Australian dollar weakness but then pulled back as shorts covered.

A much-watched speech by Treasurer Winston Peters was an anti-climax, giving the market little to move on. However, dealers said it was mildly encouraging in that Peters promised to hold the line on economic policy and gave a clear indication he would not interfere in the dollar for short-term objectives.
Dealers said any traders who had got short in the hope of Peters attempting to talk down the dollar would have been disappointed.

A comment from Alliance Party Leader Jim Anderton after his briefing from the Reserve Bank Governor Don Brash that Brash wanted the dollar lower and interest rates higher prompted some knee-jerk reaction.
But dealers said the view was not news to the market and Brash has previously acknowledged he can't do much to change the mix of monetary conditions.
